Japan's long economic downturn helped drive the trend, as drinkers looked for cheaper opportunities to drown their sorrows. Now, according to Asahi Breweries, the market for so-called "beer-like" drinks is set to grow 84% this year. Asahi is predicting profits to rise 50% in 2005 as it launches a drink based on soybean peptides rather than malt. The chosen name, "Shinnama" or "new draft", disguises its non-beer nature. But despite a record profit in 2004 of 30.6bn yen ($291m; £154m), up 31.8% on the previous year, Asahi is coming late to the market.

Specifically, we show if an orthogonal projection map satisfies certain invariance conditions, restricting to its range yields an equivalent primal-dual pair over a lower-dimensional symmetric cone---namely, the cone-of-squares of a Jordan subalgebra of symmetric matrices. We present a simple algorithm for minimizing the rank of this projection and hence the dimension of this subalgebra. We also show that minimizing rank optimizes the direct-sum decomposition of the algebra into simple ideals, yielding an optimal "block-diagonalization" of the SDP. In 1847, he helped launch L'Avenir with George Batchelor. In the same year, he also helped found the Société Mercantile d’Économie, an association for store clerks, and served as secretary. He supported annexation to the United States. In 1852, L'Avenir ceased publication. Shortly afterward, Dorion moved to Durham

These parametrized Wadge games subsume the original Wadge game, the eraser and
backtrack games as well as Semmes's tree games. In particular, we propose that
the lower cones in the Weihrauch degrees are the answer to Andretta's question
on which classes of functions admit game characterizations.

every (transfinite) level of the Baire hierarchy via an iteration of a pruning
derivative on countably branching trees.

This paper introduces an extended version of the Linear Temporal Logic (LTL)
graphical interface. It is a sketch based interface built on the Android
platform which makes the LTL control interface more straightforward and
friendly to nonexpert users. By predefining a set of areas of interest, this
interface can quickly and efficiently create plans that satisfy extended plan
goals in LTL. The interface can also allow users to customize the paths for
this plan by sketching a set of reference trajectories. Given the custom paths
by the user, the LTL specification and the environment, the interface generates
a plan balancing the customized paths and the LTL specifications. We also show
experimental results with the implemented interface.

Models trained with AGs implicitly learn to suppress irrelevant regions in an input image while highlighting salient features useful for a specific task. This enables us to eliminate the necessity of using explicit external tissue/organ localisation modules of cascaded convolutional neural networks (CNNs). AGs can be easily integrated into standard CNN architectures such as the U-Net model with minimal computational overhead while increasing the model sensitivity and prediction accuracy. The proposed Attention U-Net architecture is evaluated on two large CT abdominal datasets for multi-class image segmentation. Experimental results show that AGs consistently improve the prediction performance

Image normalization is a building block in medical image analysis. Conventional approaches are customarily utilized on a per-dataset basis. This strategy, however, prevents the current normalization algorithms from fully exploiting the complex joint information available across multiple datasets. The evolution of schizophrenia refers to the theory of natural selection working in favor of selecting traits that are characteristic of the disorder. Positive symptoms are features that are not present in healthy individuals but appear as a result of the disease process. These include visual and/or auditory hallucinations, delusions, paranoia, and major thought disorders. Negative symptoms refer to features that are normally present but are reduced or absent as a result of the disease process, including social withdrawal, apathy, anhedonia, alogia, and behavioral perseveration. Cognitive symptoms of schizophrenia involve disturbances in executive functions, working memory impairment, and inability to sustain attention. We study the spontaneous emission from a regular lateral array or a randomly
distributed ensemble of quantum dots under strong excitation (full inversion)
conditions. We focus on the similarities and differences between the cases of
random and regular arrangement of the dots and show that there is very little
difference between the evolution of luminescence in these two cases, both for
identical dots and for a realistically inhomogeneously broadened ensemble. This
means that the enhanced emission or superradiance effect is not due to
accidental clustering of pairs of dots. Moreover, we point out that observation
of an enhanced emission under weak excitation does not prove that true
superradiance will develop in a fully inverted system.

Given a natural language expression and an image/video, the goal of referring segmentation is to produce the pixel-level masks of the entities described by the subject of the expression. Previous approaches tackle this problem by implicit feature interaction and fusion between visual and linguistic modalities in a one-stage manner. However, human tends to solve the referring problem in a progressive manner based on informative words in the expression, i.e., first roughly locating candidate entities and then distinguishing the target one. In this paper, we propose a Cross-Modal Progressive Comprehension (CMPC) scheme to effectively mimic human behaviors and implement it as a CMPC-I (Image) module and a CMPC-V (Video) module to improve referring image and video segmentation models. Permutations that avoid given patterns have been studied in great depth for their connections to other fields of mathematics, computer science, and biology. From a combinatorial perspective, permutation patterns have served as a unifying interpretation that relates a vast array of combinatorial structures. In this paper, we introduce the notion of patterns in inversion sequences. A sequence $(e_1,e_2,\ldots,e_n)$ is an inversion sequence if $0 \leq e_i<i$ for all $i \in [n]$. Inversion sequences of length $n$ are in bijection with permutations of length $n$; an inversion sequence can be obtained from any permutation $\pi=\pi_1\pi_2\ldots \pi_n$ by setting $e_i = |\{j \ | \ j < i \ {\rm and} \ \pi_j > \pi_i \}|$. To date, it has only been accomplished for two centres in crystalline solids: phosphorus in silicon using electrical readout based on a single electron transistor (SET) and nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond using optical readout. A spin readout fidelity of about 90% has been demonstrated with both electrical readout and optical readout, however, the thermal limitations of the electrical readout and the poor photon collection efficiency of the optical readout hinder achieving the high fidelity required for quantum information applications. eleven-dimensional supergravity on eight-manifolds $M$ down to $\mathrm{AdS}_3$
spaces for the case when the internal part $\xi$ of the supersymmetry generator
is chiral on some proper subset ${\cal W}$ of $M$. In this case, a topological
no-go theorem implies that the complement $M\setminus {\cal W}$ must be a dense

form.

Deglaciation is the transition from full glacial conditions during ice ages, to warm interglacials, characterized by global warming and sea level rise due to change in continental ice volume. Thus, it refers to the retreat of a glacier, an ice sheet or frozen surface layer, and the resulting exposure of the Earth's surface. The decline of the cryosphere due to ablation can occur on any scale from global to localized to a particular glacier. After the Last Glacial Maximum (ca. 21,000 years ago), the last deglaciation begun, which lasted until the early Holocene. Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL or ATLL) is a rare cancer of the immune system's T-cells caused by human T cell leukemia/lymphotropic virus type 1 (HTLV-1). All ATL cells contain integrated HTLV-1 provirus further supporting that causal role of the virus in the cause of the neoplasm. A small amount of HTLV-1 individuals progress to develop ATL with a long latency period between infection and ATL development. ATL is categorized into 4 subtypes: acute, smoldering, lymphoma-type, chronic. Acute and Lymphoma-type are known to particularity be aggressive with poorer prognosis. Biography Hondo was born in 1936 in Ain Oul Beri Mathar in the Atar region of Mauritania. His mother was Mauritanian and his father Senegalese. In 1954 Hondo went to Rabat, Morocco, to train to become a chef at the International Hotel School there. He emigrated to France in 1959 and found work first in Marseille and then in Paris, variously as a cook, farm labourer, waiter, dockworker and delivery man.

short current pulses in the period-amplitude plane. For a wide parameter range

there is a multimodal transition between the set of odd modes and the set of
all modes. It is located between the 2:1 and 3:1 locked-in regions. It is the
same dynamic instability as the one discovered earlier in the Hodgkin-Huxley
model and observed experimentally in squid giant axons. It appears
simultaneously with the bistability of the states 2:1 and 3:1 in the
perithreshold regime. These results imply that the multimodal transition may be
a universal property of resonant neurons.

Majesty (abbreviated HM for His Majesty or Her Majesty, oral address Your Majesty; from the Latin maiestas, meaning "greatness") is used as a manner of address by many monarchs, usually kings or queens. Where used, the style outranks the style of (Imperial/Royal) Highness, but was formerly inferior to the style of Imperial Majesty. It has cognates in many other languages, especially of Europe. Origin Originally, during the Roman republic, the word maiestas was the legal term for the supreme status and dignity of the state, to be respected above everything else. This was crucially defined by the existence of a specific case, called laesa maiestas (in later French and English law, lèse-majesté), consisting of the violation of this supreme status.

In order to generate realistic, natural-looking motions, most data-driven approaches require considerable efforts of pre-processing, including motion segmentation and annotation. Existing (semi-) automatic solutions either require hand-crafted features for motion segmentation or do not produce the semantic annotations required for motion synthesis and building large-scale motion databases. In addition, human labeled annotation data suffers from inter- and intra-labeler inconsistencies by design. We propose a semi-automatic framework for semantic segmentation of motion capture data based on supervised machine learning techniques. It first transforms a motion capture sequence into a ``motion image'' and applies a convolutional neural network for image segmentation. Dilated temporal convolutions enable the extraction of temporal information

Calmodulin (CaM) (an abbreviation for calcium-modulated protein) is a multifunctional intermediate calcium-binding messenger protein expressed in all eukaryotic cells. It is an intracellular target of the secondary messenger Ca2+, and the binding of Ca2+ is required for the activation of calmodulin. Once bound to Ca2+, calmodulin acts as part of a calcium signal transduction pathway by modifying its interactions with various target proteins such as kinases or phosphatases. Structure Calmodulin is a small, highly conserved protein that is 148 amino acids long (16.7 kDa). quantum-classical computations, such as teleportation and measurement-based

The random walker (RW) algorithm is used for both image segmentation and registration, and possesses several useful properties that make it popular in medical imaging, such as being globally optimizable, allowing user interaction, and providing uncertainty information. The RW algorithm defines a weighted graph over an image and uses the graph's Laplacian matrix to regularize its solutions. This regularization reduces to solving a large system of equations, which may be excessively time consuming in some applications, such as when interacting with a human user. Techniques have been developed that precompute eigenvectors of a Laplacian offline, after image acquisition but before any analysis, in order speed up the RW algorithm online, when segmentation or registration is being performed. Dictogloss is a language teaching technique that is used to teach grammatical structures, in which students form small groups and summarize a target-language text. First, the teacher prepares a text that contains examples of the grammatical form to be studied. The teacher reads the text to the students at normal speed while they take notes. Students then work in small groups to prepare a summary of their work using the correct grammatical structures, and finally each group presents their work to the rest of the class. We find that the Strong Monogamy Conjecture holds true in this system, with the quantum correlation between pairs of qubits never exceeding the total quantum correlation in the system. Our results provide insights into the quantum correlations in multipartite quantum systems and have implications for quantum information processing and quantum communication.

We present a stable multiscale Petrov-Galerkin finite element method for high frequency acoustic scattering from rough surfaces. The method is based on the idea of balancing the modal space of the rough surface scattering problem with carefully chosen test spaces. By introducing the concept of balanced spaces, we show that the resulting finite element method is stable, i.e., the solution of the finite element method converges to the solution of the continuous scattering problem as the mesh is refined. In addition, we develop an efficient finite element algorithm to solve the resulting linear system of equations. The efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical examples.

We introduce DeepEdge, a deep neural network specifically designed for top-down contour detection. DeepEdge performs multi-scale inference, utilizing a bifurcated architecture inspired by the human visual system to simultaneously detect multiple object scales. Our network architecture is designed to utilize the benefits of both encoder and decoder networks, which, to our knowledge, is novel in the field of object detection. We demonstrate that DeepEdge is capable of detecting contours in a wide range of scales, and that our bifurcated architecture performs optimally when compared to current state-of-the-art methods on the publicly available cluttered planar dataset.

QANet is presented as a novel quality assurance network for image segmentation tasks. The proposed framework leverages the use of deep neural networks to generate high-quality segmentations by incorporating both global and local context information. The network architecture is designed to address the unique challenges faced in image segmentation, such as class imbalance and object occlusion. Additionally, QANet incorporates a novel quality assessment mechanism that allows for the selection of the most reliable segmentation outputs. Extensive experiments on various benchmark datasets demonstrate the superior performance of QANet compared to existing state-of-the-art methods. The results suggest that QANet is a promising approach for improving the quality and accuracy of image segmentation tasks.

In this paper, we investigate the role of delta-shocks and vacuums in zero-pressure gas dynamics using the flux approximation. The flux approximation is a simplified model of gas dynamics that assumes that the flow is inviscid and that the pressure is zero. We show that in this approximation, delta-shocks, which are discontinuities in the velocity field, play a crucial role in the formation of vacuums, which are regions of zero density. We demonstrate that the formation of vacuums is a result of the interaction between delta-shocks and the density field. We prove that the formation of a vacuum is accompanied by the creation of a delta-shock, and that the propagation of a delta-shock leads to the formation of a vacuum.

The algorithm uses a simple linear programming model to estimate the weighting function for each vertex in the projection matrix. In particular, we find that the resulting PSS are robust against perturbations due to local deformations of the surfaces.

Number theory is a branch of mathematics focusing on the properties of positive integers. This paper presents a common approach to solving three open problems in number theory: the Collatz Conjecture, the Riemann Hypothesis, and the Goldbach Conjecture. Firstly, we introduce the concept of Diophantine equation and its relevance to these problems. Then, we review the current status of each problem and present our proposed approach. For the Collatz Conjecture, we prove a weaker version using modular arithmetic. For the Riemann Hypothesis, we show that a certain function satisfies certain properties that may lead to a proof or disproof. Lastly, for the Goldbach Conjecture, we prove a version for even integers and propose a strategy to prove the original conjecture.

This research presents a novel approach to semantic image segmentation using fully transformer networks. The proposed method leverages the power of transformers, which have shown promising results in natural language processing and computer vision tasks. By applying transformers directly on pixel values instead of feature maps, our model is able to capture long-range dependencies between pixels effectively. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that our fully transformer network outperforms state-of-the-art methods on several benchmark datasets, highlighting its potential as a powerful tool for semantic image segmentation.

There has been surprisingly little work on actually defining what "privacy" means in the context of differential privacy, despite the fact that this is arguably the most important concept in the field. We argue that this is because the concept as it has been commonly used is inherently vague and difficult to formalize. Alternatively, we propose to use as a definition for differential privacy the property that a mechanism $M$ preserves the marginal distribution of any differentially private query $Q$. This leads us to a new characterization of differential privacy in terms of probability distributions, which we illustrate with several examples. We also show that our proposed definition is equivalent to the standard definition through a series of technical proofs.

> We present an extension to our previously developed mesoscopic model [1] that allows us to simulate systems containing both colloids and adsorbed molecules, such as surfactants or polymers. In this work we focus on the case where the adsorption process occurs at equilibrium; however, it should be possible to extend the methodology to include non-equilibrium processes in future studies. Our approach involves modifying the interaction potential between particles so that they are repelled when their centers come within a certain distance of each other. This prevents them from overlapping and ensures that they remain well separated throughout the simulation. Additionally, we introduce a new parameter called the “adsorption strength” which controls how strongly the particles interact with one another.

The proposed approach utilizes uncertainty estimation to guide the segmentation process. First, a pre-segmentation is performed using a fully supervised deep learning model, and the resulting masks are used to estimate the uncertainty of the predicted segmentations. This uncertainty is then used to guide the refinement of the segmentations using a semi-supervised deep learning model. The proposed approach is evaluated using a dataset of OCT images and achieved high accuracy in segmenting the retinal layers while requiring significantly less training data compared to fully supervised segmentation methods. Abstract: The field of medical imaging has seen significant advancements in recent years, but the accurate segmentation of medical images remains a challenging task. In this paper, we propose a new approach for image segmentation using weak shape priors. We begin by generating a set of candidate segments using a fast marching method. We then apply a shape prior to each candidate segment, which models the expected appearance of objects in the image. The shape prior is calculated using a deep learning model trained on a large dataset of medical images. Finally, we refine the boundaries of the candidate segments using a graph cuts algorithm to produce the final segmentation. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple medical image segmentation

The GTP utilizes the geometric properties of materials to convert thermal energy into electrical energy, offering significant advantages over conventional thermoelectric devices. In this paper, we investigate the role of natural convection in the dissolution of sessile droplets. We consider a droplet of pure water with a small amount of surfactant on a smooth hydrophobic substrate. The surfactant lowers the surface tension of the water, and the droplet is thus unstable with respect to Laplace's equation. We show that, in the presence of natural convection, the droplet can be stabilized by the surfactant. The surfactant also affects the dissolution rate of the droplet, and we find that the dissolution is enhanced by the natural convection.

We consider implications of the form P(x) => Q(x), where P and Q are probability measures defined on an underlying sample space. We say that such an implication is strict (non-strict) just in case Q << P, respectively Q ~ P, which means that Q assigns a larger (smaller) probability to every event than does P. We investigate the relative entailment of such implications, i.e. the circumstance under which Q << P implies P => Q. Our basic conclusion is that this circumstance holds in a surprisingly limited range of cases.

This paper presents a novel approach to image segmentation using cellular automata. Our method utilizes the dynamic nature of cellular automata to extract meaningful features from images and partition them into distinct regions. We propose a hybrid approach that combines the advantages of both deterministic and stochastic cellular automata to achieve accurate and efficient segmentation. Our method is evaluated on a variety of images, and the results show that it can achieve state-of-the-art performance in terms of segmentation quality and speed. We believe that our approach has the potential to revolutionize the field of image segmentation and pave the way for a new generation of algorithms.

We evaluate our method on the ACDC dataset, and show that it outperforms state-of-the-art methods that use only the first slice label for segmentation.

We then review the experimental progress in flux braiding, including the experimental demonstration of flux braiding in superconducting circuits, the experimental demonstration of flux braiding in semiconductor quantum dots, and the experimental demonstration of flux braiding in cold atoms. We also discuss the challenges and future directions in flux braiding experiments.

Semantic image segmentation is a critical task in computer vision, but existing approaches often fail to capture object scales effectively. This paper proposes a novel scale-aware semantic image segmentation method that leverages multi-scale features and attention mechanisms. The proposed method addresses the challenge of scale variation in objects by learning scale-aware attention maps. These maps guide the network to focus on different scales for different objects, leading to improved segmentation accuracy. Experimental results on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving state-of-the-art performance in scale-aware semantic image segmentation. The proposed method has the potential to benefit various applications, including autonomous driving and object recognition.

Consumer spending increased by 2.3%, while exports were up 4%.

However, government investment fell sharply - down 5.8% on the previous quarter.

In this paper, we propose a new semantic image segmentation method based on dilated convolutions with lateral inhibitions. The proposed method consists of two steps: (1) feature extraction using dilated convolutions, and (2) semantic segmentation using the extracted features. The features are extracted by applying dilated convolutions with different dilation rates to the input image. The extracted features are then fed into a semantic segmentation network, which consists of a series of convolutional layers with lateral inhibitions. The lateral inhibitions are used to encourage the network to learn semantically meaningful features. The proposed method is evaluated on the PASCAL VOC 2012 semantic segmentation benchmark, and the results show that the proposed method outperforms the state-of-the-art methods.

The DCA-GCN architecture consists of multiple encoder-decoder blocks, where each block contains an encoder module that extracts features from the input images using convolutional layers with residual connections, followed by a decoder module that generates the output masks using transposed convolutions and upsampling operations.
